description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, marked at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, also on a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy, shown in blue with circle markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 0.93 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86 and remains relatively stable, ending at around 0.94 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00; Δ Accuracy, depicted in orange with diamond markers and a dashed line style, begins at about 0.3 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, decreases to around 0.1 at an Initial Confidence of 0.93, and then slightly increases to approximately 0.15 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00; Initial Accuracy, represented in green with square markers and a dashed line style, starts at roughly 0.4 at an Initial Confidence of 0.86, increases to around 0.9 at an Initial Confidence of 0.93, and then remains relatively stable before decreasing to approximately 0.8 at an Initial Confidence of 1.00.
